hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to high-contrast, curved boundaries that define the silhouette of a large, rounded, or volumetric mass against a background of opposing luminosity. The activating feature is typically a bulbous, spherical, or domed shape—such as a helmet, shoulder, toilet bowl, celestial body, or liquid droplet—or a distinct curved shadow, rendered in deep charcoal or pitch black contrasting against bright white or light gray. The neuron remains invariant to the polarity of the contrast (responding to both light-on-dark and dark-on-light), surface texture (ranging from smooth plastic to coarse fur or liquid), and object identity, provided the sharp tonal separation and convex curvature are preserved. The activating form typically occupies 30–70% of the image area, often dominating a specific quadrant or bisecting the frame with a prominent diagonal or arcing edge.
